reason: This Hebrew text passage from Exodus 14 focuses entirely on God's instructions to Moses regarding the Israelites' camp positioning, Pharaoh's decision to pursue them, and the miraculous parting and crossing of the Red Sea. The narrative describes events and God's directives but contains no account of the Hebrew people voicing complaints or dissatisfaction about their leaders (Moses or others). The only mention of crying out is God asking Moses 'Why do you cry out to Me?' (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה מַה־ תִּצְעַק אֵלָי), which refers to Moses appealing to God rather than the people complaining about leadership. The passage culminates with the successful crossing and the destruction of the Egyptian army with no complaints from the Israelites recorded.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
